results.evidence: No outside source states a car-to-car gain for Arriva alone. A 4-day Arriva+Fisher trip logged 11,200 ft gain/loss over 18.5 mi, and a one-day Arriva+Fisher push logged about 11,000 ft over 20 mi; both include Fisher Peak. The stored 4,500 is clearly too low against the itinerary (9,900) and those reports, but no source gives the Arriva-only figure, and computing one is not allowed.

results.fact: Day-1 gain/loss vs its own note
results.evidence: The note lists only the main segments; the day's own gain includes the ups and downs through the basin. A 2019 trip report gives exactly '7.4 hours + 5600 feet from TH' to Upper Silent Lake, matching the stored hours and gainFt.

Waypoints and itinerary put the summit ~7.2 mi one way while dist_km says 5.0 mi. No outside source gives a one-way figure for Arriva: the NPS gives 3.5 mi to Easy Pass only, and the trip reports give round-trip totals (18.5 mi, 20 mi) that include Fisher Peak. No external source agrees with a specific one-way value, so dist_km is left alone.

results.correct_value: Peak and everything beyond Easy Pass are in North Cascades National Park; the trailhead and trail up to the pass are Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
results.evidence: Wikipedia places Mount Arriva in North Cascades National Park. The NPS Easy Pass/Fisher Creek trail page and the Forest Service trail page both treat Easy Pass as the forest/park boundary, and the 2019 trip report describes the Silent Lakes trip as inside the park.

patches.replace: The trailhead and the trail up to Easy Pass are Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District); everything beyond the pass, including Fisher Creek Basin, Silent Lakes and the peak, is inside North Cascades National Park.

results.fact: How to get the wilderness permit
results.correct_value: Reserve on recreation.gov and request the permit by email no more than 3 days before the start date (walk-up permits in person at a permit station the day before or day of); no trailhead self-issue, and in-person Marblemount pickup applies only to Cascade River Road trailheads
results.evidence: The NPS permits page says reservation holders request permits by email no more than 3 days before departure, walk-up permits are issued in person the day before or day of, and only Cascade River Road trailheads require in-person pickup in Marblemount; it mentions no self-issue and no 11am deadline. WTA and the Washington's National Park Fund describe the same email process starting in 2025. So the waypoint's self-issue claim and the 11am Marblemount pickup in ACCESS and the itinerary are all wrong.

results.fact: Line from Fisher Creek Basin to the notch
results.evidence: The waypoints are a sparser set that omits the Silent Lakes stop rather than describing a different line: the notch pin's note ('rising traverse across a talus bowl') matches the approach's final segment, and trip reports place a ~7,600-7,800 ft notch/col on the south/southwest ridge reached by a traverse from the Silent Lakes side. Adding pins is out of scope.

results.correct_value: Usually a multi-day trip with a camp at Silent Lakes (full overnight pack); a one-day car-to-car push is done only by fast parties
results.evidence: A 2019 trip report did Arriva over four days from a Silent Lakes camp, the peak's route page notes most groups camp at Silent Lakes, and a WTA report describes a multi-day Silent Lakes trip. A 2022 report shows a one-day push is possible (13 hours, with Fisher Peak) but is the exception. PARTNER REQUIREMENTS calling a light day pack 'typical' is the outlier.

patches.expect: Light single-push day pack (roughly 15-25 lbs) is typical; heavier if bivying to break up the long approach
patches.value: Most parties carry a full overnight pack to camp at Silent Lakes; a light day pack (roughly 15-25 lbs) suits only fast parties doing the whole trip car-to-car in one very long day

patches.find: commonly done car-to-car in one long day or broken with a basin camp

results.correct_value: No pets at Easy Pass or anywhere in the park
results.evidence: The NPS Easy Pass/Fisher Creek page says pets are not allowed at Easy Pass or anywhere else in the national park, so access.rules is correct. Other hiking pages say dogs are allowed only up to the boundary at the top of the pass. The wrong wording is in bivy[1].notes ('as far as the pass'), which is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch is written here.
